mechanism_narrative: A high current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces corporate credit availability and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals aggressive monetary tightening, which reduces corporate borrowing costs and economic growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the labor force (PAYEMS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% and 0.2% monthly growth rates, respectively, signals an overheating economy that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL growth > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL growth > 0.2% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a high level of industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its historical trend indicates an economy approaching capacity constraints, triggering monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO is above 100 (index 2017=100).

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that accelerates wage growth and inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts level (HOUST) exceeding 1300 thousand units signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level indicates restrictive monetary policy, which suppresses short-term equity market activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeding 1.5% in the prior 6 months signals sustained economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 1.5% in 6 months.
